facts.statement: Lourinhanosaurus was a carnivorous theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Lourinhanosaurus (meaning "Lourinhã lizard") was a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur

facts.statement: The first remains of Lourinhanosaurus were found in 1982 near Lourinhã, Portugal, but the genus was not described until 1998 by Octávio Mateus.
facts.quote: Its first remains were found at Peralta, near Lourinhã, Portugal in 1982, but were not described until 1998, by Portuguese paleontologist Octávio Mateus

facts.statement: The only known species, L. antunesi, was named in honor of paleontologist Miguel Telles Antunes.
facts.quote: Its type (and to date only) species is L. antunesi, in honour of Portuguese paleontologist Miguel Telles Antunes

facts.statement: The most complete known specimen is the holotype ML 370, a partial skeleton.
facts.quote: To date, the most complete known specimen of L. antunesi is the holotype, ML 370, which is a partial skeleton

facts.statement: Around 100 eggs, some containing embryonic bones and skin, were found in 1993 at the beach of Paimogo.
facts.quote: Besides these specimens, around 100 eggs (collectively described as specimen ML 565), some of them containing embryonic bones and skin, have been found in 1993 at the nearby beach of Paimogo

facts.statement: Lourinhanosaurus is estimated to have been 4 to 6 meters in length.
facts.quote: L. antunesi is estimated to be 4-6 m in length

facts.statement: Lourinhanosaurus was the first theropod dinosaur for which gastroliths were definitively assigned to the animal.
facts.quote: this was the first theropod dinosaur for which this kind of remains have been assigned

facts.statement: There is no firm scientific consensus on the classification of Lourinhanosaurus.
facts.quote: The relationships of Lourinhanosaurus to other theropods have been uncertain, and no firm consensus has been reached as to its classification

facts.statement: Lourinhanosaurus was initially considered a primitive member of Allosauroidea and later discussed as closely related to Sinraptoridae.
facts.quote: Initially regarded as a primitive member of Allosauroidea, it was later discussed as being closely related to Sinraptoridae (Metriacanthosauridae), a more inclusive clade within Allosauroidea

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Lourinhanosaurus may not be an allosauroid but rather a member of the more basal group Megalosauroidea.
facts.quote: Since the original description, some researchers have been favourable to the idea that L. antunesi is not even an allosauroid, but in fact a member of Megalosauroidea, a more basal group of tetanuran theropods

facts.statement: A 2012 study by Carrano et al. classified Lourinhanosaurus as a coelurosaur.
facts.quote: Carrano et al. (2012) found it to be a coelurosaur

facts.statement: A 2022 study refers to Lourinhanosaurus as a putative metriacanthosaurid.
facts.quote: A 2022 study mentions it as a "putative metriacanthosaurid"

facts.statement: Lourinhanosaurus is tentatively placed within the superfamily Allosauroidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: ¿Allosauroidea?

facts.statement: Lourinhanosaurus lived approximately 150 to 145 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 150 y 145 millones de años, en el Kimmeridgiense y el Titoniense

facts.statement: Lourinhanosaurus was a moderately large carnivorous dinosaur.
facts.quote: Lourinhanosaurus era un dinosaurio carnívoro medianamente grande

facts.statement: The discovered specimen was a subadult measuring about 4.5 meters in length and weighing around 160 kilograms.
facts.quote: El espécimen encontrado era un subadulto, midiendo cerca de 4,5 metros de largo y alcanzando alrededor los 160 kilogramos

facts.statement: The partial skeleton ML 370 includes six cervical vertebrae with ribs, five sacral vertebrae with ribs, 14 caudal vertebrae, eight chevrons, both femurs, the right tibia and fibula, one metatarsus, both ilia, pubes, ischia, and 32 associated gastroliths.
facts.quote: Este esqueleto parcial, ML 370, consiste de los restos de seis vértebras cervicales con sus costillas, cinco vértebras sacras con las costillas, 14 caudales, ocho cheurones, ambos fémures, tibia y fábula derecha, un metatarso, ambos íliones, pubis e isquiones, y asociados a ellos 32 gastrolitos

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests Lourinhanosaurus formed nesting colonies on a floodplain.
facts.quote: Estos restos indican que dichos terópodos se congregaron en una llanura de inundación formando colonias de anidación

facts.statement: Researchers estimate that at least six females laid eggs simultaneously in an area of only 32 square meters.
facts.quote: Se estimó que dichos huevos fueron puestos por al menos 6 hembras, todos de forma simultánea, en un área de tan sólo 32 metros cuadrados

facts.statement: There is no evidence that Lourinhanosaurus excavated nests or buried eggs; they likely laid them directly on the ground in a sunny spot near a pond.
facts.quote: No existen evidencias de que se excavaran nidos ni se enterraran los huevos, así que lo más probable es que fueran puestos directamente sobre el suelo en un lugar soleado al borde de algún estanque

facts.statement: It is probable that Lourinhanosaurus did not actively incubate its eggs.
facts.quote: Es probable que los huevos no fueran empollados activamente

facts.statement: Lourinhanosaurus lived from 152.21 to 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 145.06 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Lourinhanosaurus lived in Portugal during the Late Jurassic Period.
rejected.quote: It lived during the Late Jurassic Period (Kimmeridgian/Tithonian) in Portugal
rejected.reason: quote not found verbatim in the source

rejected.quote: Histology shows that the holotype specimen was between 14 and 17 years old
